scope: Conditional dynamical feasibility and primary-literature review; no new equilibrium/wind/MHD/observer solution.
status: Executed scales, limitations and candidate ranking complete.

density20p19.scope: Illustrative D from the companion frozen-bath probe, not inferred density or new atomic solution.

ranking.candidate: Slow dense sector with an explicit force balance and solved excitation
ranking.reason: Closed magnetic topology or an external-pressure boundary can alter density and residence time without requiring the whole sphere to carry a larger mass flux.

ranking.candidate: Joint density and directional irradiation/thermal response
ranking.reason: More density can supply n2 but also recombination-fed emission, opacity and thermal/radiative feedback. Neither low n3/n2 nor a darker disk is guaranteed.

ranking.status: Lower-priority parameterization until geometry and thermal support are specified
ranking.reason: Volume filling factor, projected covering and optical depth are distinct; transit morphology does not establish coverage at dayside emission phases.

disfavored_shortcuts: Adding a spherical tidal acceleration already present in the saved driver.
Inferring n2 enhancement directly from a gas-density multiplier or from the free shape speed alone.
Lowering mass loss at fixed speed to increase density.
Using beta=1 as proof of closed stable confinement or as a detected magnetic field.
Treating a clumping factor as an opacity-only multiplier or a known projected covering factor.
not_evaluated: Nonideal MHD and field topology/stellar boundary.
A new momentum/energy/charge/statistical-equilibrium solution at the proposed density.
Self-consistent optical-depth feedback, observer halo emission and native residual/Q.
Formation and survival of clumps or time-dependent supply.

independent_review.result: PASS: rho reconstruction, continuity/ram scaling, beta and dipole scaling, microclump versus covering distinction, and Hill directional surface equations. No substantive inconsistency found.
